stories.note: Copy prompt works, shows Copied. Hero gives no sign-up cue. Clipboard contents not verified (browser blocks read).
Pricing reachable in 1 click, Start with Free goes to /sign-up. Clerk form not-walkable. Banner uses self-host wording.
Clerk sign-up not walkable. Console loading card and onboarding panel walked with test session; copy mismatch with real approve flow.
Whole detour walked, recovery download not verifiable headless. Connect an agent dialog has invisible Copy button.
Failure card and Try again recovery work. Dismiss leaves permanent loading card. Real hotel wifi simulated by aborting /api/console.
Clerk sign-up not walkable. CLI login, connect page errors, approval, console, check ok all walked. Needed /api suffix on API URL.
Landing, FAQ, docs, llms.txt, quickstart read. Contradictions about sign-up and recovery file found.
Not-configured panels and signed-out /console redirect observed on this local server; dead end confirmed.

findings.description: The Copy button inside the Connect an agent dialog is invisible: computed color rgb(17,17,17) with transparent background on the dark (#111) code block. It is present at x816 y403 (49x28) and in the a11y tree as 'Copy agent instruction'. Also invisible at 390px.
findings.expected: Visible Copy button like the orange one in the onboarding panel
findings.actual: Dark code block with no visible control; user must select text by hand
findings.suggested_fix: Give the dialog copy button the same light/orange styling as the onboarding Copy

findings.description: On the 'Workspace unavailable' state, clicking Dismiss on the red error line changes the card to 'Opening your workspace...' which never resolves and has no Try again button, even after the network recovers. Only the Refresh button or reload fixes it. Reproduced twice.
findings.expected: Dismiss only hides the message, or the card keeps its Try again button
findings.suggested_fix: Track failure state separately from the dismissible error text

findings.description: Failure shows the same message twice (red line next to the title and the card text) and three recovery controls: Dismiss, Refresh and Try again. Card says 'refresh to try again' while its button says Try again. On mobile the error appears as an unstyled bar flush to the screen edge.
findings.expected: One message, one recovery action
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the header error when the card is showing, reword card to 'Try again'

findings.description: The landing hero, closing section and console panel never tell a new user that the approval link requires sign-up/sign-in. llms.txt tells the human 'you must be signed in' and its troubleshooting says 'they must sign in first'; only docs/quickstart.md starts with 'Sign up'. A brand-new human only finds out at /connect, where the only sign-up cue is the small 'New here? Sign up free' line.
findings.expected: Copy that says you will create an account on the next screen
findings.actual: 'Free to start. Your agent shows a pairing code, and you approve it in your account.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'You will sign up when your agent shows the link' to hero and llms.txt tell-the-human line

findings.description: Onboarding panel, landing hero, quickstart and the Connect dialog say the human just clicks Approve / 'You approve it once'. The real page requires typing a 16-character Verification code and the button is 'Approve agent'. A first-time user is not prepared for the extra step.
findings.expected: Copy mentions checking the code and typing the verification code
findings.evidence: SETUP-003 screenshots/step-3-onboarding.png vs SETUP-006 screenshots/step-2.png and step-3-empty-code.png
findings.suggested_fix: Change to 'open it, type the verification code your agent printed, and approve'

findings.description: A brand-new account with no drive sees 'Set a passphrase and agents will add every drive's key to your account...' next to the Files title and a 'Set up' link that opens a Set up passphrase unlock dialog with a generated passphrase and 'every drive must be added again' warning. This competes with the primary 'Connect your agent' action before any drive or agent exists, and uses jargon. On mobile the banner is hidden so the 'Key needed . Not backed up' chip is unexplained.
findings.expected: Passphrase prompt only after a drive exists
findings.suggested_fix: Hide until first drive; show a short explanation on the chip on mobile

findings.description: With AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL=http://localhost:3811 (no /api) the CLI prints only 'Agent Drive refused the login request: 404'. It does not say which URL was tried or that the API URL should end in /api. llms.txt uses --api .../api, so it works there. After a working login the CLI also prints 'Ignored a different API URL returned by the server.' with no explanation.
findings.expected: Error names the URL and suggests the /api path
findings.evidence: CLI output: 'Agent Drive refused the login request: 404'; 'Ignored a different API URL returned by the server.'
findings.suggested_fix: Include the request URL and a hint in the 404 message; explain or drop the ignored-URL line

findings.description: After sign-out, /console redirects to plain /sign-in with no redirect_url, while /connect keeps it. Confirmed at runtime. Also the approval page shows the account only inside collapsed Details (here 'Local test session'), so a user already signed in to another account may approve into the wrong one.
findings.expected: Return path kept; account shown near Approve
findings.evidence: SETUP-006 screenshots/step-2.png and step-2b-details.png; SETUP-005 sign-out check ended at http://localhost:3811/sign-in
findings.suggested_fix: Pass redirect_url for console routes; show account line outside Details

findings.description: Receipt dialog repeats 'Without it nobody, including us, can open this drive' twice, has no close button, and the New drive dialog checkbox 'Agent-only - never add this drive to passphrase unlock' uses a term the user has not met. After 'I saved it' the drive name truncates to 'research-no...' while the Recovery file saved message occupies the toolbar. On mobile the toast is flush to the left edge. Connect dialog URL breaks mid-word ('ll/ms.txt').
findings.expected: Say each thing once; no truncation of a short drive name
findings.suggested_fix: Remove repeat, shorten toast, allow wider drive chip

findings.description: Public pricing page shows 'Paid checkout is not enabled on this deployment. The Free plan is available when sign-in and storage are configured...' and 'Overage rates have not been published for this deployment', wording for self-hosters. Developer and Team show a disabled Coming soon with no timeline. 'stored ciphertext' is unexplained. Seen on this local host where checkout is off; production wording not checked.

findings.description: FAQ 'What happens if I lose the drive key?' says to save the recovery file when you create a drive, but the agent-first path (the one the landing page promotes) never has the human create a drive. The same panel claims 'one step with no keys to paste' while the page needs a code. 'Sign up free' appears five times on the landing page, 'Copy prompt' (landing) vs 'Copy' (console) differ.

findings.description: Sign-up and sign-in not-configured panels say 'Configure the Agent Drive Clerk instance to enable human access' with no link to self-host docs and no next step; header Sign up free and Sign in loop between them. stories.note: Happy path worked end to end (llms.txt, login, approve, backup to file, skill install --target, check ok). Findings are copy inconsistencies, a cropped mobile input and small CLI messages. Not walkable: npm install, clipboard/1Password success, Chrome auto-open. The named session uxw-install-login was contaminated by another walker overwriting a shared scratchpad helper, so the first run is kept in screenshots/first-run-shared-session/ and login/approve/console were redone in session uxw-install-login-solo.

Signed-out redirect to /sign-in with redirect_url, sign-in to sign-up hop with redirect_url, manual code entry and approve walked. The Clerk sign-in/sign-up cards, email verification and whether redirect_url survives them are not-walkable (sign-in shows 'not configured on this installation').

Login with --no-browser, approve, credentials export --stdout then confirm, and a fresh home with AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS (check ok) all walked. A real Docker/CI container, EACCES on global install, real npx download, Node < 24 and CI-suppressed browser open are not-walkable. Device login was rate-limited (slow_down) for about 55 minutes before this could be walked.

CLI printed 'The login code expired. Run `agent-drive login` again.' after 10 minutes, the stale card and the fresh No pairing card both gave recovery text, and a re-run login was approved successfully. Laptop-sleep and 5-network-failure variations not walked.

Wrong verification code, incomplete code and non-code input produce clear inline errors; correct code accepted case- and space-insensitively. Confirmed there is no Deny button. Account row is only inside collapsed Details.

/llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, markdown twins and the docs link to llms.txt all work; /cli/agent-drive.tgz is 404. Findings: quickstart omits the verification code, setup section is below ~60 lines of index.

Console drive creation, recovery file download, agent and API key creation all work, and login --token-stdin saves the key. But the human-first path dead-ends: credentials import rejects the console's recovery file, and check then says 'run agent-drive login again'. Only the undocumented AGENT_DRIVE_KEY env var gets check ok. Clerk reverification and Finder not walkable.

findings.description: The CLI cannot import the recovery file that the console gives a human-first user. `credentials import --from agent-drive-<id>.key.json` fails; only adcred1 bundles are accepted and the error does not say so.
findings.expected: Import accepts the recovery file (format agent-drive-key-v1), or the error names the expected file and the working alternative.
findings.actual: Not a valid Agent Drive credentials bundle.
findings.evidence: CLI output 'Not a valid Agent Drive credentials bundle.'; recovery file format=agent-drive-key-v1; screenshots /Users/dennison/develop/agent-drive-ux-setup/docs/ux-walker/setup-nov27/stories/SETUP-015/screenshots/step-4.png
findings.suggested_fix: Accept agent-drive-key-v1 in credentials import, or point the error at AGENT_DRIVE_KEY.

findings.description: After login with an API key and no local drive key, `agent-drive check` says to run login again, which cannot fix a key-based login.
findings.expected: Tell the user to supply the drive key (recovery file or AGENT_DRIVE_KEY).
findings.actual: There is no usable drive key on this machine. Run `agent-drive login` again.
findings.evidence: CLI output of check in ~/uxw/install-login-015 on the Studio
findings.suggested_fix: Branch the message when the config came from --token-stdin or an env API key.

findings.description: Console API keys page says 'Run the CLI from the repository after building it' and shows a login command and env-var reads that differ from llms.txt/docs; it never mentions --token-stdin or the recovery file. The new-key dialog says only 'use it with agent-drive login'.
findings.expected: Same install and login commands as the docs, including --token-stdin and how to supply the drive key.
findings.actual: Developer wording and a different command shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the From your terminal block to match quickstart.

findings.description: AGENT_DRIVE_KEY and AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<DRIVE_ID> are the only working way to give the CLI a recovery-file key, but `agent-drive --help` does not list them.
findings.expected: Help lists all configuration env vars.
findings.actual: Help lists CONFIG, API_URL, API_KEY, MACHINE, CREDENTIALS only. check ok was obtained only with AGENT_DRIVE_KEY.
findings.suggested_fix: Add both variables to help and to the console snippet text.

findings.description: `login --token-stdin` success prints one line of whoami JSON with no sentence, config path or next step, and no reminder that the drive key is still missing.
findings.expected: Human summary plus the drive-key reminder.
findings.actual: Raw JSON {accountId, agentId, keyId, scopes, driveIds...}.
findings.suggested_fix: Print 'Saved API key for agent X. No drive key on this machine yet: ...'.

findings.description: The first Create a drive dialog shows 'Agent-only — never add this drive to passphrase unlock' before passphrase unlock is explained; the Files header sentence about setting a passphrase is likewise unexplained for a user with no drive.
findings.expected: Plain wording or hide under Advanced.
findings.suggested_fix: Move behind an Advanced disclosure.

findings.description: Console onboarding steps say 'The agent shows a pairing code. You approve it once.' without the verification code that the approve page requires.
findings.expected: Mention the verification code.
findings.suggested_fix: Change step 3 to 'Type the verification code and approve it once.'

findings.description: Home hero says the agent 'shows a pairing code, and you approve it', the console Agents panel says 'open it and click Approve', and the served quickstart says 'check that the code matches ... and click Approve'; /llms.txt, connect-an-agent and /connect require a second never-shown 16-hex verification code.
findings.expected: Every surface mentions the verification code.
findings.actual: Website copy mentions one code; the approve page demands another.
findings.evidence: Hero text 'Free to start. Your agent shows a pairing code, and you approve it in your account.'; console Agents panel (SETUP-009/screenshots/step-5.png context); GET /docs/quickstart.md section 3
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'type the verification code your agent prints' to hero hint, console panels and quickstart.

findings.description: At 390px width the Verification code input is about 165px wide, so the placeholder and typed 16-character code are cut off after three groups.
findings.expected: Full code visible, or label stacked above the input.
findings.actual: Placeholder reads 'a1b2 c3d4 e5f6' and the last group is hidden.
findings.suggested_fix: Stack label above input on narrow screens.

findings.description: `agent-drive skill install` with no ~/.claude or ~/.codex prints instructions but exits 0 although nothing was written.
findings.expected: Non-zero exit or explicit 'not installed'.
findings.actual: 'No ~/.claude or ~/.codex directory found. The skill is at ...; copy it to <skills dir>/agent-drive/SKILL.md, or use --target <dir>.' with rc=0
findings.suggested_fix: Exit non-zero so an agent following llms.txt step 5 does not report success.

findings.description: Login prints 'Ignored a different API URL returned by the server.' with no explanation (probably a local-origin artifact).
findings.expected: Silent, or names both URLs.
findings.actual: Unexplained warning before 'Logged in as agent ...'.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the URLs or drop the line when harmless.

findings.description: AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL set to the site origin (no /api) fails with a bare status and no URL or hint; the console snippet shows the origin-only form for --api.
findings.expected: Message naming the URL tried and the /api suffix.
findings.actual: Agent Drive refused the login request: 404
findings.suggested_fix: Include the URL and hint.

findings.description: Right after a successful agent connection, console Files says 'Ready for your first file. Connect an agent with the CLI or MCP to upload encrypted files.' with a 'Key needed · Not backed up' chip, as if no agent were connected.
findings.expected: Acknowledge the connected agent and explain the chip.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'billing-api agent is connected; its first file will appear here.'

findings.description: A signed-out visitor following an agent's approval link lands on a plain 'Sign in' screen with no mention that an agent pairing is waiting; new users must notice the orange header button or the small 'New here? Sign up free' line.
findings.expected: Context line plus equal sign-in/sign-up choices.
findings.actual: Generic Sign in heading (Clerk card not renderable here).
findings.suggested_fix: Show pending-agent context and both choices on the redirect page.

findings.description: /connect for an unknown code sends a signed-out user to sign-in first; the wrong-code message appears only after signing in.
findings.expected: Mention the 10-minute lifetime on the sign-in page.
findings.suggested_fix: Low priority.

findings.description: After entering a code manually, the URL stays /connect, so a reload loses the pairing request.
findings.expected: URL updates to /connect?code=XXXX-XXXX.
findings.evidence: agent-browser get url after Continue; SETUP-010/screenshots/step-4.png

findings.description: quickstart.md starts with 'Sign up' while /llms.txt, the surface an agent reads, has no sign-up step; the order differs.
findings.expected: One order.
findings.actual: quickstart step 1 'Create your account at /sign-up'; llms.txt only says the approval link asks the human to sign in.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'No account yet? The link lets you create one.' to llms.txt.

findings.description: When the device-login start limit (20 per IP per hour) is hit, the CLI prints only 'slow_down'. Nothing says it is a rate limit or how long to wait; shared-IP sandboxes and CI will hit this and may loop. Observed for about 55 minutes of retries.
findings.expected: A plain message with the wait time and a non-zero exit.
findings.actual: Agent Drive refused the login request: slow_down
findings.evidence: CLI output repeated on every retry 18:11 to 19:03 EST
findings.suggested_fix: Map 429 slow_down on the start call to 'Too many login attempts from this network; try again in N minutes' and use Retry-After.

findings.description: The post-login backup paragraph lists 1Password and clipboard first; for a sandbox the sensible route (export --stdout, confirm, AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS) is not in the paragraph.
findings.expected: Sandbox hint when non-interactive.
findings.suggested_fix: Add --stdout to the printed options or detect non-interactive environments.

findings.description: No time limit is shown before the request expires; the terminal prints only 'Waiting for approval...' and the page says 'the request expires on its own'.
findings.expected: 'This code works for 10 minutes'.
findings.suggested_fix: Print 'Expires in 10 minutes' in the CLI and on the card.

findings.description: A stale pairing card still shows an active Approve after expiry; clicking it shows an inline error with literal backticks around `agent-drive login`, unlike the code-styled text on the No pairing card.
findings.expected: Card flips to the expired state; consistent code styling.
findings.actual: This request expired or was already used. Run `agent-drive login` in your agent to get a new code.

findings.expected: Tell the user to copy the code as printed.
findings.actual: Format message for a well-shaped code.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to 'That is not a valid code. Copy it from your terminal.'

findings.description: One message ('wrong, expired, or already used') covers an unknown code and an already approved code, so a user who already approved cannot tell it succeeded.
findings.expected: Distinguish used, expired and unknown.
findings.actual: Same text for approved MHZL-CQMP and unknown BCDF-GHJK.

findings.expected: A secondary Deny button (the deny route exists).
findings.evidence: /Users/dennison/develop/agent-drive-ux-setup/docs/ux-walker/setup-nov27/stories/SETUP-013/screenshots/step-1.png; interactive elements: Details, checkbox, input, Approve only
findings.suggested_fix: Add Deny that calls the existing deny route.

findings.evidence: GET /docs/quickstart.md section '3. Log in and approve' vs /llms.txt step 2

findings.description: The human-facing setup guide in /llms.txt starts at line 63, about 925px down, under a long doc index; only 'The setup guide follows the lists.' points to it.
findings.expected: Setup first or a jump hint.

findings.description: llms.txt step 2 says 'Other options on the page are optional; the defaults are right.' with no reference to which options a human would see.
findings.expected: Name the options or drop the sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'Leave Details closed unless you want to limit access.'

findings.description: The header has no link to the setup guide; llms.txt is reachable only via docs, hero text and console panels.
findings.expected: Optional.
findings.actual: Header shows Pricing, Docs, Sign in, Sign up free.

stories.note: Happy path works: approval card clear, one dominant Approve, CLI finished in about 6s. Low findings: CLI says console 'Settings' but nav has none; footer 'Console, Agents' is not a link. Brief's API URL needed the /api suffix.

Bare /connect flow works (empty, vowel, wrong, correct code). Findings: at 390px the Verification code input is 168px wide so the typed code scrolls and the placeholder is cut; vowel error says 'form XXXX-XXXX' without naming letters; 'NO PAIRING' tag on plain input errors; no UI link to /connect.

Clerk sign-up/sign-in forms not walkable. Verified: signed-out redirect to /sign-in?redirect_url=..., the redirect survives the sign-in/sign-up switch (hrefs and URL), then approval as a new test user works. Quickstart, console Agents copy and home page omit the verification code.

Empty, non-hex, pasted-with-label, wrong-last-digit and hyphenated codes all behave; mismatch message is clear. Low findings: pasted 'Verification code: ...' line rejected with generic message; non-hex char not named; orphan word in error.

No Deny/Cancel control confirmed (only Approve, Details, delegate checkbox); closing the tab leaves the request pending and still approvable (I approved it later). Agents page lists no pending requests. Footer 'Console, Agents' is plain text.

Real reconnect (config still present) works with 'It reconnects to the drive it used before' and a clear 'API key changed' CLI message. But the story's persona (lost config, same name) silently creates a second same-named drive and a second key under one agent (high finding). Hit CLI 'slow_down' rate limit (20 starts/IP/hour) with no explanation; waited about 1 hour.

Existing-drive path walked with an adcred1 bundle pasted in Drive key (file chooser and console recovery-file download not exercised). Errors for garbage key and bad folder are clear. Findings: Read only + write folder accepted (CLI then prints 'Scopes: read' and 'Writes limited to: /papers'); two drives with identical names in the select; link hidden in Details and says 'recovery file'; mixed-order two-column grid; sticky Approve covers hint on mobile.

Delegate checkbox inside Details updates the summary line; ravi-lead got scope delegate; grant to worker-1 printed the approval URL; worker page shows 'offered by ravi-lead' and approval succeeded. Findings: delegate hidden in Details, done card does not confirm delegate, repeated names. 'Forgot checkbox' failure and focus re-fetch banner not walked.

Walked a real 10-minute expiry and an already-used code. Both recover with a clear command; double-click posts one approval. Low findings: literal backticks in the expired banner vs styled command on entry card; no expiry time or countdown; generic 'wrong, expired, or already used'. On-page rate-limit message and session-expiry redirect not walked.

Wrong-account detection by email not walkable (test session shows 'Local test session' for every user; no real Clerk). Confirmed no account name or sign-out control on the /connect header and the account only appears in collapsed Details; approval completes in three steps with no account confirmation.

findings.description: Logging in again with the same agent name but no saved key (the story's lost-config persona) shows 'New encrypted drive' with no notice that an agent with this name exists. After approval the account has a second drive with the same name and the one agent shows '2 ACTIVE KEYS'. The old drive is not reconnected and its key is not recovered.
findings.expected: Tell the user an agent with this name already exists and offer reconnect (with backup) or a new drive.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a notice on the page when the agent name already exists in the account.

findings.description: After about 20 login starts from one IP, the CLI prints only a bare rate-limit code with no wait time or explanation. The docs say 20 starts per IP per hour. 'slow_down' is also the polling term, so the message is misleading. The block lasted about one hour in this run.
findings.expected: A message naming the limit and when to retry.
findings.actual: CLI output: 'Agent Drive refused the login request: slow_down'
findings.evidence: CLI output quote above; docs/api-device-login.md line 54 'at most 20 starts per IP address per hour'
findings.suggested_fix: Map 429 on device_authorization to a human message with the wait.

findings.description: CLI success text says 'Set a passphrase in the console under Settings' but the console sidebar has no Settings item; the only route is a small 'Set up' link in the Files header.
findings.expected: CLI names a control the user can see.
findings.actual: Mismatch between CLI wording and console UI.
findings.evidence: docs/ux-walker/setup-nov27/stories/SETUP-016/screenshots/step-4.png; CLI line 'Set a passphrase in the console under Settings; agents will add the drive then.'
findings.suggested_fix: Change CLI text to 'click Set up on the Files page' or add a Settings entry.

findings.description: The served quickstart (docs/quickstart.md line 35), the console Agents panel ('open it and click Approve') and the home page ('shows a pairing code') omit the verification code that the approval page requires. Only llms.txt and connect-an-agent.md mention it.
findings.expected: Every surface describing approval says to type the verification code.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'and type the verification code your agent printed' to those texts.

findings.description: There is no Deny or Cancel control on the approval page. A user who does not recognise the request can only close the tab; the CLI keeps 'Waiting for approval...' and the request stays approvable until it expires (I approved a closed-tab request later to confirm).
findings.expected: A visible Deny button using the existing deny route.
findings.actual: Only Approve; small grey text says to close the page.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a secondary Deny button.

findings.description: Console Agents page lists no pending pairing requests ('0 AGENTS / Create your first agent') while one is outstanding, so a request cannot be reviewed or cancelled there.
findings.expected: Pending requests with a cancel action.
findings.suggested_fix: List pending requests.

findings.description: The /connect header has no account name or sign-out control, and the account appears only in the collapsed Details row. A user with two accounts can approve into the wrong one in three steps; the done card does not name the account. Email text could not be checked: the test session shows 'Local test session' for every user.
findings.expected: Show 'Approving as <email>' with a 'Not you?' link on the card and the done card.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the account under the title and on the done card.

findings.description: Read only plus 'Only allow writes under /papers' is accepted; the agent then logs in with 'Scopes: read' and 'Writes limited to: /papers', and the done card does not mention the folder.
findings.expected: Folder field disabled or explained when Read only is ticked.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable the folder field when Read only is checked.

findings.description: Drive select lists two drives with the same name ('luis-claude' and 'luis-claude (Dennisons-Mac-Studio.local)') with no id or date, so the wrong drive's key could be handed over.
findings.expected: Distinguishing detail such as short id.
findings.suggested_fix: Append short id or created date.

findings.description: 'Use one of my drives instead (needs its recovery file)' is a small link inside collapsed Details and says 'recovery file' although a pasted key or adcred1 bundle also works.
findings.expected: Visible entry with wording that matches what is accepted.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to 'Use one of my existing drives'.

findings.description: In the existing-drive form 'Or choose a file' sits under the folder field in the right column while the Drive key is in the left column; the Drive key placeholder is clipped ('Paste the drive key or a'). Clicking Approve on an empty form shows only the verification code error, not the missing key.

findings.description: At 390px wide the Verification code input is 168px wide because its label sits beside it. The placeholder is cut to 'a1b2 c3d4 e5f6' and a typed code shows only its last three groups, so the user cannot check the typed value. Same layout on SETUP-023 and SETUP-025.

findings.suggested_fix: Stack the label above the input below about 480px.

findings.description: Vowels typed in the pairing code field are accepted and shown, then Continue says 'Enter the code in the form XXXX-XXXX.' The form is right; the allowed letters are never named. The tag also changes to 'NO PAIRING' on plain input errors, and the wrong/expired/used message cannot tell a typo from an expired code.
findings.expected: Drop invalid letters or name them; keep AWAITING CODE until a lookup fails.

findings.description: No link to /connect exists in the header or console nav; a user with the agent on another machine must know the URL.
findings.expected: Route reachable from the console Agents panel.
findings.suggested_fix: Link /connect from the Agents panel.

findings.description: A pasted 'Verification code: 9fb7 99bc 8b49 1723' line, or a code with a non-hex character (l or o), gets the generic 'four groups' message that names neither the label nor the allowed characters. The error also wraps with an orphan '7890.'.
findings.expected: Accept the pasted line or say 'use only 0-9 and a-f'.
findings.actual: Enter the verification code your agent printed, as four groups like a1b2 c3d4 e5f6 7890.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip a leading label and name the allowed characters.

findings.description: The delegate option is inside collapsed Details. An orchestrator user sees nothing on the main card. The done card does not confirm 'can add other agents' even though the summary line did.
findings.expected: Visible or pre-requestable option; done card confirms delegate.
findings.suggested_fix: Let login request delegate; repeat it on the done card.

findings.description: The worker request summary reads 'ravi-lead · can read and write · offered by ravi-lead' because drive and agent share a name; the same word appears three times.
findings.expected: Labelled parts, e.g. Drive and Offered by.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the parts.

findings.description: The expired banner shows literal backticks around agent-drive login, while the entry-card message styles it as code. The open page after expiry keeps a live-looking form with no expiry time or countdown; the entry card message lumps wrong, expired and already used.
findings.expected: One wording and styling; an expiry time on the page.
findings.actual: Two wordings; user learns of expiry only after typing the code.

findings.description: With Details open the Approve agent button falls below the 800px fold (the delegate hint and rows push it down); Requested shows a bare US-locale timestamp with no timezone. The signed-out sign-in page gives no context about the waiting approval.
findings.expected: Primary action visible; time with timezone.
findings.suggested_fix: Compact Details rows; show relative expiry.

findings.description: If AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL lacks the /api suffix (as the walk brief had it), the CLI prints only 'Agent Drive refused the login request: 404' with no hint. The brief's URL had to be changed to http://localhost:3811/api. Also the footer 'Console, Agents' text on the approval card is not a link.
findings.expected: Message names the URL called or says the URL should end in /api.
findings.actual: Agent Drive refused the login request: 404
findings.suggested_fix: Include the URL and a hint on 404.

stories.note: CLI steps pass (check refusal, confirm, status, check ok). Clipboard copy and Apple Passwords paste not walkable: headless Studio, pbcopy fails. Stood in with export --stdout then confirm.
check refusal, file export and check ok all work. Run on the SETUP-026 agent, because a second device login was rate-limited. ~/Documents export fails with no reason when the folder is missing.
op-not-installed error and file fallback walked. op install, signed-out and vault-locked states, and the 1Password app paste are not walkable. The home already had a stdout backup recorded.

put, get, cmp, share, share list, revoke and the error cases all pass in the CLI. Share page, revoked page and missing-key page walked. The browser download failed because the page fetches from 127.0.0.1:9811, which is unreachable from my browser. Console folderUrl and share dialog not walked.

A read-only agent needs a delegate-scope device login. Login was rate-limited for the whole session: slow_down, 20 starts per IP per hour across all walkers. The delegate-scope error text was observed and is clear.
skill install walked with no ~/.claude or ~/.codex, plus --target variants. Findings on DIR layout, llms.txt vs quickstart order, no Cursor guidance, exit 0 when nothing is written.

CLI parts covered via the sibling stories. Console chip, unlock dialog and passphrase steps not walked: shared browser cookie overwritten by other walkers, second login rate-limited, download host unreachable. New-user console empty state walked at 1280 and 390.

export --stdout piped, confirm, then three fresh homes using only AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS. whoami, check ok, put and ls all work. Bundle supplies the API URL. Secret store and CI secret UI not walkable. TTY refusal observed with ssh -tt.

findings.description: Device login start is limited to 20 per IP per hour. The CLI reports only 'slow_down', with no explanation or wait time. A team behind one NAT or a CI fleet gets stuck at the first step. This blocked SETUP-030 and SETUP-032 here.
findings.expected: A sentence explaining the limit and when to retry
findings.actual: Agent Drive refused the login request: slow_down
findings.evidence: CLI login output repeated for about 35 minutes; docs/api-device-login.md says 20 starts per IP per hour
findings.suggested_fix: Map slow_down on device_authorization to plain text with the wait time.

findings.description: With AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL set to the bare origin (as instructed), login fails with an unhelpful 404. Adding /api works but prints 'Ignored a different API URL returned by the server.' The instruction supplied for this run was wrong; the CLI error does not hint at it.
findings.expected: Hint that the URL should end in /api, or tolerate a bare origin
findings.actual: Agent Drive refused the login request: 404
findings.suggested_fix: On 404 suggest the /api suffix.

findings.description: After login the terminal prints the backup hint and then a second instruction: set a passphrase in the console under Settings. A first-timer sees two next steps, and the backup is the one that blocks check.
findings.expected: One clear next step
findings.actual: 'Back up this agent's credentials...' followed by 'Your account has no account key yet... Set a passphrase in the console under Settings'
findings.suggested_fix: Number the backup as step 1 and mark the passphrase optional or later.

findings.description: The approved page tells the user to return to the agent but never says a credentials backup is still required before check passes.
findings.expected: Mention the backup
findings.actual: Return to your agent to finish setup and confirm it is ready.
findings.suggested_fix: Add that the agent will ask where to store the key backup.

findings.description: A clipboard backup confirmed with `credentials confirm` is recorded and reported as method stdout. The user never used stdout.
findings.expected: Method says clipboard or manual
findings.actual: Recorded the credential backup for 1 drive(s) (stdout).
findings.evidence: CLI confirm output; credentials status method:stdout
findings.suggested_fix: Record clipboard when the pending export came from --to clipboard.

findings.description: A bare `credentials export` error lists only --to <path> or --stdout, hiding the 1password and clipboard targets that help and llms.txt lead with.
findings.expected: The error lists all targets
findings.suggested_fix: Print the usage line or name all four targets.

findings.description: The clipboard failure error offers 1password or a file but not the --stdout | STORE && confirm route.
findings.expected: Include the stdout route
findings.actual: Could not copy to the clipboard with pbcopy. Nothing was exported. Use `--to 1password` or `--to <a file outside the repo>` instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the stdout route.

findings.description: Exporting to ~/Documents/... when the Documents folder does not exist fails with no reason or recovery step. The story's own example path hits this on Linux and containers.
findings.expected: Say the folder does not exist and how to fix it, or create parent folders
findings.suggested_fix: Create parent directories, or report the cause.

findings.description: The check refusal lists three backup routes with no recommended default for a user who wants to finish quickly.
findings.expected: One suggested next command
findings.suggested_fix: Lead with one command, then the alternatives.

findings.description: check --drive <unknown> says no key exists on this machine and does not point to whoami or login.
findings.expected: A recovery hint
findings.actual: There is no key for drive 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 on this machine.
findings.suggested_fix: Append: run agent-drive whoami to see usable drives.

findings.description: When the 1Password CLI is missing, the error only says how to install it. It does not say that clipboard-and-confirm or a file also work, which is the hesitation in the story.
findings.expected: The error ends with the clipboard and file alternatives
findings.actual: The 1Password CLI (`op`) is not installed. Nothing was exported. Install the 1Password CLI (https://developer.1password.com/docs/cli/get-started/), turn on its desktop-app integration ... then run this again.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the clipboard and file alternatives to the op errors.

findings.description: The file backup success line does not name the file written or warn against repo and synced folders.
findings.expected: Backed up credentials for 1 drive(s) to <absolute path> (file)
findings.suggested_fix: Print the absolute path and a one-line safety note.

findings.description: The third backup route is worded differently by surface: help says 'outside the repo', the login hint and docs say 'outside the sandbox'.
findings.expected: One phrase
findings.actual: help: 'a file outside the repo'; BACKUP_HINT: 'a file outside the sandbox, on a path that survives it'
findings.evidence: CLI help vs login hint vs clipboard error
findings.suggested_fix: Unify the wording.

findings.description: On the 'Share unavailable' card the Try again button and the Go to Agent Drive link touch, with no gap, at desktop and mobile.
findings.expected: A 12-16px gap
findings.actual: Button right edge and link left edge are both at x=500
findings.suggested_fix: Add a gap to the action row.

findings.description: The --expires-in error for 90s does not give the min or max or say seconds are unsupported. The story text expected a 'between 2m and 30d' message.
findings.expected: The range in the message
findings.actual: --expires-in must use a duration such as 30m, 24h, or 7d.
findings.suggested_fix: State the units (m, h, d) and the range.

findings.description: Re-put to an existing path suggests merging and --if-version and never mentions --overwrite, which is what a user replacing a file wants.
findings.expected: Mention --overwrite
findings.actual: The file already exists. Current version: <id>. Read the file again, merge your change, then retry with --if-version <id>.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: or pass --overwrite to replace it.

findings.description: The share download card keeps an empty status area under the Download button, which leaves about 50px of dead space in the card.
findings.expected: A tight card
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse the empty status region.

findings.description: Browser download was not walkable. The page fetched the ciphertext from 127.0.0.1:9811 (local object store), unreachable from the browser. The user sees 'The file could not be downloaded. Check your connection and try again.'
findings.expected: The download starts
findings.suggested_fix: Test-environment only; verify on staging.

findings.description: The read-only reviewer path needs a delegating agent and a fresh device login. With the per-IP login limit hit, the CLI says only slow_down. The story could not be walked.
findings.expected: Explain the login limit
findings.actual: Agent Drive refused the login request: slow_down
findings.suggested_fix: See SETUP-027-F4.

findings.description: llms.txt makes skill install a required step 5 before check. The quickstart lists it as 'Optional' step 7 after check. An agent and a human following different surfaces get different setups.
findings.expected: One order and one optionality
findings.actual: llms.txt: '5. Install the skill...' before '6. Check that it worked'; quickstart: '## 7. Optional: skill and MCP'
findings.suggested_fix: Make both say optional and after check.

findings.description: --target DIR writes DIR/SKILL.md, while claude and codex write skills/agent-drive/SKILL.md. --target ./.cursor/skills produces a layout agents will not find, and the CLI help does not say so.
findings.expected: Help says DIR is the final skill folder
findings.suggested_fix: Say in help that DIR is the folder that will contain SKILL.md, or append agent-drive.

findings.description: Nothing says where Cursor or other agents read skills. The no-folder message only tells the user to copy the file by hand.
findings.expected: Name common folders or point to MCP
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line pointing to MCP or to the folder the agent reads.

findings.description: skill install exits 0 when nothing was written, so scripts cannot detect the miss.
findings.expected: A non-zero exit or an explicit status
findings.suggested_fix: Exit non-zero or print 'nothing installed'.

findings.description: A repeat skill install overwrites silently with the same 'wrote' line, and `skill --help` prints the entire CLI help.
findings.expected: 'Updated' wording and skill-specific usage
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'updated' when the file existed.

findings.description: A brand-new console shows the passphrase banner ('Set a passphrase and agents will add every drive's key... Set up') above the 'Give your first agent a home' card, before any agent or drive exists. Two calls to action compete, and nothing mentions the credentials backup that check requires.
findings.expected: One next step (connect an agent)
findings.actual: Header banner with a Set up button plus the connect card
findings.suggested_fix: Hide the passphrase banner until a drive exists.

findings.description: Console chip and unlock steps were not walkable. Other walkers overwrote the shared test-session cookie, so the console showed another persona's drive and an unrelated Capture dialog. A second device login was rate-limited, and the download host was unreachable.
findings.expected: An isolated run
findings.evidence: Console snapshot during the SETUP-026 walk
findings.suggested_fix: Re-walk in isolation.

findings.description: The docs and the TTY refusal imply --stdout is safe, but an agent's shell is not a terminal. An unpiped `credentials export --stdout` prints the bundle into the agent transcript with no warning.
findings.expected: The docs warn agents to always pipe, or the CLI guards the unpiped case
findings.actual: A non-TTY run printed the 417-byte bundle
findings.evidence: CLI: export --stdout | wc -c gave 417; docs/sandboxes.md says '--stdout prints the bundle only when stdout is not a terminal'; ssh -tt run was refused
findings.suggested_fix: State plainly: always pipe to a store, never run it bare in an agent shell.

findings.description: Invalid and empty bundle errors give no recovery step. The empty case does not name AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS.
findings.expected: A recovery hint
findings.actual: 'AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS is not a valid credentials bundle.' and, for an empty value, 'API configuration is missing. Run `agent-drive login` ...'
findings.suggested_fix: Add: copy the full line from your secret store (it starts adcred1.).

findings.description: The clipboard failure in a sandbox says 'outside the repo', where sandbox docs say 'outside the sandbox'. It does not mention the --stdout route.
findings.expected: Consistent wording plus the stdout route
findings.actual: Use `--to 1password` or `--to <a file outside the repo>` instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Unify the wording.

stories.note: Walked console create-drive, receipt, recovery download, chip menu, mobile, CLI login and /connect approval with own drive (pasted key; file picker unavailable). Works end to end. Findings: connect path hidden in Details, drive name truncation, CLI still says 'not backed up' and 'set a passphrase under Settings' after approval, key-box styling, no close on receipt. Earlier attempts disturbed by dev-server reloads that wiped the in-tab key (harness).

Walked passphrase setup, chip menu, Load-key dialog, CLI seal unverified, wrong-code error, seal success, Settings count. Used an equivalent agent (device login rate-limited). Not walkable: Clerk prompt, final file render (storage URL 127.0.0.1:9811 unreachable from laptop browser). Key issues: CLI sends user to 'Settings' that does not exist by that name; dialog does not include the fingerprint; chip says Unlocked before any drive is added.

Fingerprint is plain prose with trailing comma and no copy button; CLI rejects the comma with a generic message but accepts hyphens, capitals and no spaces. Env var and wrong-command errors are clear. Medium findings on error wording and 'Settings' naming.

Passkey device prompt, Clerk reverification and second laptop cannot run headless. Walked dialog, wrong-passphrase error, and found that the 'Adding passkey...' state hangs with no Esc/X/cancel until reload.

Walked wrong-passphrase, recovery-file loop, key menu Forgot link, reset dialog, silent switch to new setup, new fingerprint and 0 drives. Not walkable: Clerk prompt and the agent re-pin steps (login rate-limited). Findings: no Forgot link in the unlock dialog, disabled danger button rendered at full opacity, no message after reset.

Walked Key needed chip, Load key dialog (no passphrase), wrong-file and wrong-drive bundle errors, CLI credentials export (mode 600, check ok). Success path with a matching exported file not walkable (no agent with a console drive key; login rate-limited). Slower seal route presented before the fast export route.

Walked agent-only drive creation, receipt, chip text after reload, drive menu, Load key dialog. Not walkable: agent login/approve with own drive, account seal 'agent-only', choosing saved file (login rate-limited, no manage scope for CLI drive create). Wrong copy 'ask the agent that created this drive'; chip stays green Unlocked; no agent-only marker.

Walked generated and own-passphrase forms, length and mismatch validation, success notice. Clerk reverification cancel/retry steps not walkable with the test session. 'correct horse battery staple 2026' accepted; black password inputs; disabled Create weaker than adjacent secondary.

Walked default-ticked 'Keep this browser unlocked', Lock vs Lock this browser, reload behaviour. Confirmed: Lock then reload silently restores Unlocked; Lock this browser persists; unticked unlock stays locked after reload; setup stores key without asking. Idle 30 min lock not walked.

findings.description: 'Lock' only locks the tab; after reload the chip is Unlocked again with no prompt. 'Lock' and 'Lock this browser' are adjacent with no explanation.
findings.expected: Difference explained, or Lock clears the stored key.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename buttons ('Lock for now' / 'Lock and forget on this browser') or make Lock clear the stored key.

findings.description: 'Keep this browser unlocked' is ticked by default with no consequence text; passphrase setup stores the key in the browser with no checkbox at all.
findings.expected: Shared-computer warning or default off; same question in setup.
findings.actual: Reload after setup shows Unlocked; dialog says 'The keys stay in this browser only.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Leave unticked on a shared computer' and show the box in setup.
findings.surface: console unlock dialog and passphrase setup

findings.description: CLI says set the passphrase 'in the console under Settings' but /console/settings is titled 'Activity & deletion' and only shows 'Not set up. Manage in Files'; the word Settings appears nowhere.
findings.expected: CLI/dialogs point to Files > Set up, or Settings holds the form.
findings.actual: User is sent to a page that sends them back to Files.
findings.evidence: /Users/dennison/develop/agent-drive-ux-setup/docs/ux-walker/setup-nov27/stories/SETUP-035/screenshots/step-2.png; CLI: 'Set a passphrase in the console under Settings; agents will add the drive then.'

findings.description: No path to reset from the Unlock dialog; 'Use a recovery file instead' leads to a dialog that says the passphrase opens the drive and offers 'Use my passphrase instead' (loop). Reset exists only as the last item in the chip menu.
findings.expected: 'Forgot your passphrase?' link in the Unlock dialog.
findings.actual: Unlock dialog has only Unlock and Use a recovery file instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the link; make the agent hint conditional.

findings.description: 'Reset and remove all drives' is disabled until RESET is typed but renders at full opacity solid red; lowercase 'reset' keeps it disabled with no message.
findings.expected: Disabled style and a case hint.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply disabled style to danger buttons; accept any case.

findings.description: After reset the dialog silently becomes 'Set up passphrase unlock'; no message confirms the reset or says agents must re-pin the new fingerprint with account seal --repin.
findings.expected: Confirmation plus next step with the new fingerprint.
findings.actual: Notice only says 'Passphrase set up. Your agent can now add its drives to your account.'
findings.suggested_fix: Show reset confirmation and repin command.

findings.description: Reset copy ('removes every drive from it' next to 'Files are not deleted', 'loading its recovery file') confuses users with no recovery file.
findings.expected: Plain wording about what stays and what must be re-added.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite copy.

findings.description: After saving the console recovery file and approving the agent with that drive, the CLI still says the drive key is not backed up and 'Set a passphrase in the console under Settings'.
findings.expected: Backup records agree or the difference is explained.
findings.actual: agent-drive check: 'drive key not backed up: da137623-dc1b-4ef2-8623-e3fa0e17455a' plus export hint.
findings.suggested_fix: Record console backup when the agent receives the key or explain separate records.

findings.description: 'Use one of my drives instead (needs its recovery file)' is hidden inside collapsed Details as a small underlined link; label says recovery file while the form also accepts a pasted key.
findings.expected: Visible choice for owners who created a drive themselves.
findings.suggested_fix: Surface outside Details; say 'recovery file or key'.

findings.description: If the tab reloads before the receipt is finished, the drive stays as an empty shell with chip 'Key needed - Not backed up' and no message that the key is lost.
findings.expected: Warning or recovery guidance.
findings.actual: Silent 'Key needed' state (observed after an unplanned dev-server reload).
findings.suggested_fix: Warn on unload while receipt is open; notice on never-backed-up drives without a key.

findings.description: Load-key dialog tells the owner to copy the fingerprint from Settings by hand though the console knows it; the copied seal command lacks --fingerprint so the first seal ends 'unverified'.
findings.expected: Copied command includes the fingerprint.
findings.actual: '<id>: unverified' with exit 1, then a second command is needed.
findings.evidence: /Users/dennison/develop/agent-drive-ux-setup/docs/ux-walker/setup-nov27/stories/SETUP-035/screenshots/step-8.png; CLI: 'The account key has not been verified on this machine...'
findings.suggested_fix: Embed the fingerprint in the copied command.

findings.description: Using the login 'Verification code' as the fingerprint gives 'does not match the account key the service returned (799c c0f8 98db 81e2)... the API may be answering with a different account key', which echoes the real value and blames the API.

findings.evidence: CLI: The supplied fingerprint (442c 93ea debb 6aa5) does not match the account key the service returned (799c c0f8 98db 81e2).

findings.description: After setup the chip says green 'Unlocked' and 'Drives you added to your account open when you use them' although no drive has been added; first file click opens a Load-key dialog.
findings.expected: Chip reflects passphrase ready, 0 drives added.
findings.suggested_fix: Show added-drive state.

findings.description: A fingerprint with a trailing comma is rejected with a generic message that does not name the comma, though the console sentence puts a comma after the fingerprint.
findings.expected: Trim punctuation or name the comma.
findings.actual: --fingerprint must look like "a1b2 c3d4 e5f6 7890", exactly as the console shows it.

findings.description: CLI and dialogs name 'Settings' but the page is titled 'Activity & deletion' and the passphrase card sits under the activity table.

findings.actual: Settings is not a visible label.

findings.description: Fingerprint is small grey prose with no Copy button and wraps mid-value on a phone.

findings.description: 'Adding passkey...' state cannot be closed (Esc and X ignored), shows no device-prompt hint and hung 40+ seconds when no prompt appeared.

findings.description: Dialog title and button both read 'Add a passkey'; passphrase re-entry is required with no reason given.

findings.description: With no passphrase, the Load-key dialog lists the slower account-seal route first and the quick 'credentials export then choose the file' route last.

findings.description: Dialog never says that without any copy of the key the files can never be decrypted.

findings.description: Wrong-file error is longer than docs quote; 'Choose recovery file' label does not say a credentials export is accepted.

findings.description: Agent-only checkbox uses unexplained terms and does not say the drive will always need its recovery file.

findings.description: 'correct horse battery staple 2026' is accepted without warning while the dialog claims it catches obvious patterns; mismatch is reported before strength so errors arrive one at a time.

findings.description: Passphrase inputs are solid black boxes with no placeholder; disabled Create is paler than the adjacent secondary button.

findings.description: Setup dialog and success notice never say what the passphrase does or that the agent needs the fingerprint next; notice assumes an agent exists.

findings.description: Drive picker truncates names (research-notes -> 'research-no...', second-drive, client-exports) at 1280px with spare toolbar room; seen in 034, 035, 040.
findings.expected: Full name.

findings.description: Revealed drive key sits in a 76px black box for one line; Copy button is about 2px below it.

findings.description: /connect existing-drive form interleaves columns: write-path field beside Drive select, Drive key beside Choose a file; label wraps two lines; Drive key placeholder clipped.

stories.note: Landing hero, Copy prompt ('Copied' feedback) and mobile work cleanly; npm name matches docs. Gaps: hero says 'pairing code' only, no Node 24 note or next command, inconsistent copy button styles. Covers SETUP-001 and the start of SETUP-009.

/pricing is clear and clean at 1280 and 390. Start with Free goes to /sign-up. Landing plan table says downloads 5GB/100GB/1TB; /pricing says 'Downloads not charged'. Signed-out Choose Developer keeps the return path but lands on a generic sign-in. Covers SETUP-002.

Docs, quickstart, connect-an-agent, CLI, trace capture and llms.txt render cleanly. Package name and install command match on every surface and on the npm registry (0.5.1, node >=24). Copy conflicts: quickstart omits the verification code that llms.txt and connect-an-agent require; quickstart step 4 is written to the agent. The sandboxes page screenshot timed out, so it was read as text only. Covers SETUP-007, SETUP-009, SETUP-014 reading.

/sign-up, /sign-in and bare /connect (signed out) viewed only, no form touched; clean at both sizes. Bare /connect gives no explanation. Signed-in /connect, code entry, Approve and the return after sign-up were not walked (would need an account). Covers SETUP-006 signed-out part.

Finder download link found only inside /docs/cli (GitHub release zip 'Agent Drive Finder 0.3.1'); nothing downloaded. No landing, footer or docs-index mention; /desktop, /download, /finder, /app, /mac, /docs/mount, /docs/desktop, /docs/finder return 404. The CLI page calls the app 'signed' and then says the build workflow does not sign or notarize.

findings.description: Landing plan table and /pricing disagree on downloads.
findings.expected: One download policy on every surface.
findings.actual: Landing row 'Downloads / month' shows 5 GB / 100 GB / 1 TB; /pricing says 'Downloads not charged' on all plans and 'Extra GB downloaded: Not charged'.
findings.evidence: /Users/dennison/develop/agent-drive-ux-setup/docs/ux-walker/setup-nov27/stories/PROD-02/screenshots/step-2-full.png; landing snapshot cells 5 GB, 100 GB, 1 TB; /pricing text 'Downloads not charged'
findings.suggested_fix: Make the landing table match /pricing, or the reverse.

findings.description: Hero and quickstart describe the approval step differently from llms.txt and Connect an agent. The hero says 'Your agent shows a pairing code, and you approve it'; quickstart step 3 says 'check that the code matches ... and click Approve'. llms.txt and /docs/connect-an-agent require typing a separate verification code.
findings.expected: Every surface mentions the verification code the human must type.
findings.actual: A human who reads only the hero or quickstart hears about one code, then meets a required second field on /connect.
findings.evidence: /Users/dennison/develop/agent-drive-ux-setup/docs/ux-walker/setup-nov27/stories/PROD-01/screenshots/step-1.png; quickstart: 'check that the code matches the one in the terminal, and click Approve'; connect-an-agent: 'types the verification code into the page'
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'type the verification code the agent prints' to the hero hint and quickstart step 3.

findings.description: Quickstart step 4 is addressed to the agent ('Offer these choices in this order and let the person pick one') on a page that says 'This page walks you through'. Step 1 'Sign up' also differs from the agent path in llms.txt, where sign-up is not a step.
findings.expected: Instructions addressed to the reader.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword step 4 for the human reader and note that sign-up can happen when the approval link asks for sign-in.

findings.description: The macOS Finder app is not discoverable. Landing, footer, docs index, sidebar and llms.txt never mention it, and guessed URLs return 404. The only download link (GitHub release zip 'Agent Drive Finder 0.3.1') is inside two paragraphs of the 48 KB CLI reference.
findings.expected: A visitor who wants Finder access finds a page and a download from the nav or docs index.
findings.actual: Reachable only by reading the CLI reference sections 'Install and configuration' and 'macOS requirements and unmounting'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Finder and mounts' docs page to the docs index and link it from the landing page.

findings.description: The CLI reference contradicts itself on whether the Finder app is signed. It says 'the separate signed Agent Drive app', then says the macOS builder workflow 'compiles the app but does not sign, notarize, or publish it'. A new user cannot tell whether macOS will warn about an unidentified developer.
findings.expected: One clear statement of signing and notarization state and what the user sees on first open.
findings.actual: Both claims appear in the same paragraph.
findings.evidence: /Users/dennison/develop/agent-drive-ux-setup/docs/ux-walker/setup-nov27/stories/PROD-05/screenshots/step-1-cli-macos.png; /docs/cli paragraph starting 'The Linux npm package includes native mount helpers'
findings.suggested_fix: State whether the 0.3.1 zip is signed and notarized, and separate that from the source-build workflow.

findings.description: The hero terminal option shows the npm install command with no Node 24 requirement and no next command (agent-drive login). Node 24 appears only in quickstart, llms.txt and the CLI docs.
findings.expected: The hero tells a terminal user the Node requirement and what to run next.
findings.actual: A user on an older Node runs the copied command with no warning on the page; the package declares engines node >=24.0.0.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Node 24+' and a link to the quickstart next to the hero command.

findings.description: The two hero copy controls look unrelated: 'Copy prompt' is a sentence-case outlined button in the dark panel, 'COPY COMMAND' is a small uppercase monospace outlined box.
findings.expected: Same control, same style.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one copy button style.

findings.description: Signed-out 'Choose Developer' goes to /console/billing, then to /sign-in?redirect_url=https://agentdrive.xyz/console/billing. The return path is kept, but the form says 'Welcome back! Please sign in to continue' with no mention of billing, and new visitors see 'Welcome back'.
findings.expected: A context line such as 'Sign in to choose a plan' and a prominent sign-up route for new visitors.
findings.actual: Generic sign-in; sign-up is a small link under the card.
findings.suggested_fix: Show context from redirect_url and offer 'New here? Create an account' prominently.

findings.description: Bare /connect while signed out shows the ordinary sign-in form with no explanation that this is the agent approval page or that the agent's code is needed next. The signed-in bare /connect was not walked.
findings.expected: A line such as 'Sign in to connect an agent'.
findings.actual: Identical to /sign-in; only the header links carry redirect_url=%2Fconnect.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a context line on sign-in when redirect_url is /connect.

findings.description: 'Agent setup guide' (footer and docs index) opens /llms.txt as plain monospace text that begins with a 50-line docs index; the setup steps start below the first screen.
findings.expected: Setup steps first, or a pointer to them.
findings.actual: Index first, '## Set up (local agent with a shell)' further down.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the setup section above the doc index, or label the link 'Agent instructions (plain text)'.

findings.description: Sign-up repeats the sign-in link three times: header 'Sign in', card footer 'Already have an account? Sign in', and the line below the card.
findings.expected: Say once.
findings.actual: Three links to the same destination on one screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the line below the card or keep only the Clerk footer.
